Simulate gBOIN-ET Trials

Source: R/gboin_et_simulate.R
gboin_et_simulate.Rd

Run the gBOIN-ET dose-finding algorithm of Takeda, Morita and Taguri (2022) over many simulated trials, for toxicity and efficacy outcomes with several categories that each carry a score, and return the patients, their categories and the total scores at every dose. This is the simulation engine behind sim_gboin_et, exposed for users who want the raw trial data.

Usage

gboin_et_simulate(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_grade,
  p_resp_grade,
  score,
  score_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = NULL,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  lambda1 = NULL,
  lambda2 = NULL,
  eta1 = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.99,
  p_eli = NULL,
  p_eli_resp = NULL,
  resp_cor = 0.2,
  boinet_compatible = FALSE,
  prior = rep(1/6, 6),
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target value of the mean normalized toxicity score, for example 0.47 / 1.5 for a target equivalent toxicity score of 0.47 with a largest score of 1.5.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Target value of the mean normalized efficacy score, for example 0.95 / 1.5 for a target equivalent efficacy score of 0.95 with a largest score of 1.5.

p_grade

Numeric matrix. True probability of each toxicity category (rows) at each dose (columns, in increasing dose order). Every column sums to 1. The first row is the category without a toxicity event.

p_resp_grade

Numeric matrix with one column per dose. True probability of each efficacy category (rows). Every column sums to 1. The first row is the category without an efficacy event.

score

Numeric vector, one value per row of p_grade. Score of each toxicity category, for example c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5) for grades 0 or 1, 2, 3 and 4. The scores are divided by their maximum.

score_resp

Numeric vector, one value per row of p_resp_grade. Score of each efficacy category, for example c(0, 1, 1.5) for stable or progressive disease, partial response and complete response. The scores are divided by their maximum.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort. A vector shorter than n_cohort is padded with its last element and a longer one is truncated.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level for the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar or NULL. The trial stops once this many patients have been treated at any dose. Defaults to NULL, the maximum sample size, which is the default of the 'boinet' package.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.1 * target, the value recommended by Takeda et al. (2018), which is far below the 0.6 * target of the BOIN design.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

p_saf_resp

Numeric scalar. Highest response probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target_resp.

lambda1, lambda2, eta1

Numeric scalars or NULL. Boundaries of the mean toxicity score and of the mean efficacy score. Defaults to NULL, the boundaries of boin_et_boundary for the targets. Give all three to use other values, such as those printed in an article.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its DLT rate is below p_eli falls below 1 - cutoff_eli. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is above p_eli_resp falls below 1 - cutoff_eli_resp. Defaults to 0.99.

p_eli

Numeric scalar or NULL. DLT probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses target as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.40 with a cutoff of 0.90.

p_eli_resp

Numeric scalar or NULL. Response probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses p_saf_resp as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.20 with a cutoff of 0.90.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar strictly between -1 and 1. Correlation of the Gaussian copula that links the toxicity event and the efficacy event of a patient. Defaults to 0.2, the default of the 'boinet' package.

boinet_compatible

Logical scalar. Apply the rules of the 'boinet' package (version 1.6.0) exactly. Defaults to FALSE, which keeps to Takeda et al. (2018), who do not allow dose skipping during escalation; see Details.

prior

Numeric vector of length 6. Prior probabilities of the six hypotheses. Defaults to rep(1 / 6, 6), the noninformative choice of the article. The third hypothesis, under which every decision is correct, does not enter the criterion.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. When NULL the current state of the random number generator is used. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class boin_et_trials, which is a list with components

n_pts

Integer matrix, n_trials by number of doses, of patients treated.

n_tox

Numeric matrix of the same shape: the total of the normalized toxicity scores of the patients treated at each dose.

n_resp

Numeric matrix of the same shape: the total of the normalized efficacy scores.

n_grade

Integer array, n_trials by doses by toxicity categories, of the patients in each category.

n_resp_grade

Integer array, n_trials by doses by efficacy categories. The categories take the row names of p_grade and p_resp_grade when every row has one, and G1, G2, ... and R1, R2, ... otherwise.

cohorts_used

Integer vector of cohorts enrolled in each trial.

stop_reason

Character vector giving why each trial ended.

early_stop

Logical vector, TRUE for the trials stopped early, which select no OBD.

design

"gBOIN-ET".

boundary

The boundaries used, an object of class boin_et_boundary.

settings

List of the design parameters, with the true mean normalized scores of each dose in p_true and p_resp.

Details

The gBOIN-ET design is the BOIN-ET design for ordinal outcomes. Every toxicity category and every efficacy category carries a score, such as the equivalent toxicity score and the equivalent efficacy score of the article. The scores divided by their maximum lie between 0 and 1 and are treated like fractional DLTs and responses (quasi-Bernoulli outcomes): the mean normalized scores of the patients at the current dose take the place of the observed DLT and response rates in the rules of boin_et_simulate. With pt and pe the mean toxicity and efficacy scores at the current dose, the design

  • escalates when pt <= lambda1 and pe <= eta1,

  • stays when pt < lambda2 and pe > eta1,

  • de-escalates when pt >= lambda2,

  • and otherwise moves to the dose with the highest mean efficacy score among the current dose and its neighbors, an untried higher dose being preferred and ties being broken at random.

A dose is excluded when the posterior probability that its mean toxicity score is below p_eli falls below 1 - cutoff_eli, or when the posterior probability that its mean efficacy score is above p_eli_resp falls below 1 - cutoff_eli_resp; the posterior distribution of a mean score with total x among n patients is Beta(1 + x, 1 + n - x). How the next dose is found among the admissible doses, when the trial ends, and how the rules differ from those of 'boinet' unless boinet_compatible is TRUE is described in boin_et_simulate; with boinet_compatible = TRUE the rules are those of boinet::gboinet().

target, target_resp and the other design parameters are on the normalized scale. The boundaries of boin_et_boundary come from a grid in steps of 0.01 that starts at p_saf, target and p_saf_resp, so that they depend on the decimals of the targets: the targets 0.47 / 1.5 and 0.95 / 1.5 give 0.1413, 0.3733 and 0.50, the values used by Takeda et al. (2022), who print 0.14, 0.37 and 0.50. The mean scores are not multiples of 1 / n, so boundaries rounded to two decimals can give other decisions; lambda1, lambda2 and eta1 take the boundaries of an article directly.

A patient has a toxicity event when the toxicity category is not the first one, and an efficacy event likewise. The two events are linked by a Gaussian copula with correlation resp_cor, and the category of a patient with an event is drawn from the probabilities of the categories above the first, independently of everything else, which is the joint distribution of boinet::gboinet(). Each patient draws one uniform variate for the toxicity event, one for the efficacy event, and one more for each outcome with more than two categories; a tie under the rule for the neighboring doses draws one more. With two categories of scores 0 and 1 for both outcomes the trials are, for the same seed, those of boin_et_simulate. The 'boinet' package draws its random numbers differently, so the trials agree with it in distribution, not one by one.

The mean score of a dose is computed as the total of the scores as given, divided by the largest score times the number of patients. With scores that are binary fractions, such as 0, 0.5, 1 and 1.5, the total is exact, so that two doses whose mean scores are equal as fractions tie, and the trials are the same on every platform. Scores such as 0.1 are not exact in floating point, and doses with equal mean scores may then fail to tie.

Possible values of stop_reason are those of boin_et_simulate.

References

Takeda, K., Morita, S. and Taguri, M. (2022). gBOIN-ET: The generalized Bayesian optimal interval design for optimal dose-finding accounting for ordinal graded efficacy and toxicity in early clinical trials. Biometrical Journal, 64(7), 1178-1191. doi:10.1002/bimj.202100263

Yamaguchi, Y., Takeda, K. and Maruo, K. (2025). boinet: An R Package for Bayesian Optimal Interval Design for Dose Finding Based on Both Efficacy and Toxicity Outcomes. The R Journal, 17(2), 15-34. doi:10.32614/RJ-2025-012

See also

sim_gboin_et, gboin_et_select_obd, boin_et_simulate

Examples

# Toxicity grades 0 or 1, 2, 3 and 4, and stable or progressive disease,
# partial response and complete response, at four doses
p_grade <- rbind(
  c(0.83, 0.62, 0.51, 0.34),
  c(0.12, 0.18, 0.19, 0.16),
  c(0.04, 0.11, 0.14, 0.15),
  c(0.01, 0.09, 0.16, 0.35)
)
p_resp_grade <- rbind(
  c(0.90, 0.50, 0.30, 0.25),
  c(0.05, 0.35, 0.20, 0.20),
  c(0.05, 0.15, 0.50, 0.55)
)
trials <- gboin_et_simulate(
  target = 0.47 / 1.5, target_resp = 0.95 / 1.5,
  p_grade = p_grade, p_resp_grade = p_resp_grade,
  score = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5), score_resp = c(0, 1, 1.5),
  n_cohort = 10, cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 200, seed = 123
)
trials
#> Simulated gBOIN-ET trials
#>   trials               : 200
#>   doses                : 4
#>   target toxicity score: 0.3133333
#>   target efficacy score: 0.6333333
#>   cohorts              : 10 of size 3
#>   max sample size      : 30
#> 
#> Average per trial:
#>                   DL1   DL2   DL3  DL4
#> Patients treated 4.41 10.66 13.24 1.35
#> Toxicity score   0.37  2.33  4.22 0.74
#> Efficacy score   0.43  3.99  8.38 0.94
#> 
#> Stopping reason (%):
#> 
#>              max_cohorts       no_admissible_dose no_lower_admissible_dose 
#>                       97                        1                        2 

# Patients of the first trial by dose and toxicity category
trials$n_grade[1, , ]
#>     G1 G2 G3 G4
#> DL1  3  0  0  0
#> DL2  2  0  1  0
#> DL3  7  6  0  2
#> DL4  5  0  0  4
